customer_wants: A $145.00 cast-alloy stand pot arrived as a housewarming present with no receipt and no order in her name, and she wants it returned for store credit.
why_legitimate: There is no record of sale on this account at all - the purchaser was somebody else and paid on their own card - so section 13's no-record-of-sale rule applies rather than the ordinary return path.
$145.00 is over the $100 no-record-of-sale ceiling a T1 agent may settle. The agent may not decide it and may not refuse it: RETURNS_T2 owns anything over that ceiling, on any tender.
Nothing else on the case is in doubt. The item is sealed, the model and finish match a live SKU, the account is four years old with no returns in the trailing 90 days and no section 8 hold.

This fixture asserts an ESCALATION as its positive, and it asserts it on a DIFFERENT TRIGGER from ORD-08. ORD-08 escalates because the amount is above band; this one escalates because there is no sale to refund against. A policy that learns 'escalate above $150' and stops there leaves this case with no correct move, and the agent has to hand it to a person for a reason that has nothing to do with the amount.

order.item_description: Cast alloy stand pot, 5.5 quart, oat white - gift, no sale on this account

input_turns: My sister-in-law gave us a stand pot for the house and it's lovely, it's just the fourth one in this kitchen. I'd like to bring it back for credit.
I don't have a receipt and it won't be under my name - she bought it on her own card and I'm not going to ask her what she paid.
It's sealed, the sleeve is still on it. I'm not after cash, store credit is completely fine.

args.note: ORD-6870, no record of sale on this account, gift from a third-party purchaser. Item sealed and identified against a live SKU at $145.00.
